about: The look: the display transform applied once per film to the rendered frames (film-language/dimensions.json 'look'). It changes no number the renderer computed. 'neutral' is a byte-identical copy. Any other look needs Erick's ruling and is recorded here with his words. Exposure policy is separate: it is written into the frame list (column 16, EXPOSURE=) before the render by look.js exposure, so the renderer itself exposes consistently; the mapping from the policy to the renderer's EXPOSURE scale is to be calibrated on one shot first (calibration row below).

film_stock_rich.what: saturation 1.1, true blacks, slightly steeper curve

warm_1_8.what: white point toward amber (colortemperature 5200 K from 6500)

exposure.about: policies for the EXPOSURE value written per frame line. 'auto' = today's per-frame EXPOSE=auto (column untouched). 'fixed' = one value for the shot. 'smooth' = a value from the Sun's true altitude (column 5) by the table below, linearly interpolated, so the exposure follows the light continuously instead of per frame.
exposure.calibration: NOT DONE: render one shot (A_axis_5s) with EXPOSURE fixed at three values and compare mean luma to EXPOSE=auto's; then fill the table so 'smooth' reproduces auto's average level without its per-frame jumps.
exposure.note: the second number is the renderer's EXPOSURE scale (default 200 per the study); placeholders until calibrated
